symptom: On the after-startup runner (every Docker run, `--local --legacy-runner`) two tests in one file that define the same variable with `retrieve $x`, `declare $x`, a list operation or aggregate (`$x = head(…)`, `$x = count(…)`), `send rest request`, `execute database query` or a loop iterator fail injection with MDL063 (MDL052 for the iterator), CE0111 "Duplicate variable name" from mxbuild. Measured by sweeping every non-.fail test file through GenerateTestRunner + ValidateProgram: setup-annotation.test.mdl (`retrieve $Brands` x3) and 1103-test-file-checks-as-microflow-bodies.test.mdl (`retrieve $Request` + `$Request = head(…)`) failed; the endpoint runner was never affected
cause: The runner joins every test into one microflow and renames each test's variables with `_N`, but the rename set came from `assignPattern`, a regex matching `$x = call|create` only. Every other way to define a variable kept its name and was declared once per test
file: `cmd/mxcli/testrunner/generator.go` (`extractVariableNames` now parses the body and takes `executor.FlowDefinedVariables`, new in `mdl/executor/validate_microflow_ce_gaps.go`); `generator_endpoint.go` (`bodyParsePrefix`, shared with `attachOnError`)
insight: Ask the validator what a body defines instead of keeping a second list: `statementProducedVars` (reflective on `OutputVariable`, plus declare/create/create list/retrieve/loop iterator) walked with `ast.StatementBodies` is exactly what MDL063 counts, so the rename set and the gate cannot drift. The wrong turn the previous finding suggested is `visitor.FlowStatements`: it yields grammar-rule names and offsets, not variable names, so it would need a hand-kept list of producing rules, a regex by another name. Sweep on MDL052 as well as MDL063: a reused loop iterator is CE0111 but reported by MDL052, and a sweep filtered on MDL063 alone shows it green. Over-renaming costs nothing (a void call's output, a String contains/find the builder turns into Change Variable) while under-renaming is CE0111, so the rename set deliberately skips MDL063's type-dependent exemptions. `$x = …` without `set` is a Change Variable (setStatement is the last alternative), not a definition, and keeps the old \b guard's intent for free. The sweep is now a test (TestLegacyRunnerRepositoryTestFilesDefineEachVariableOnce); control: the regex restored fails 15 shape cases and 3 repository files with MDL063/MDL052
